---
title: "Blind Checkpoint VII — Word Equations, Inverse Strings, Wheeler/RLBWT, Tree Strings, SL2(Fp) & Morphic Words"
subtitle: "Part VII Blind Diagnostic Assessment (Chapters 26–30 · Decoy Elimination & Untagged Contest Triage)"
---

In Parts I through VI, our primary objects were linear strings analyzed through periodicity, Lyndon factorizations, suffix automata, palindromic trees, convolutions, or subsequence matrices. In **Part VII (`Ch 26`–`Ch 30`)**, problems step beyond a single flat string: they present systems of **word equations and lexicographical inequalities**, **Eulerian and Wheeler automaton graphs**, **tree-path strings and stack-cancellation groups**, or **infinite Sturmian, Thue–Morse, and morphic words** at lengths up to $N \le 10^{18}$.

In a live contest, these problems arrive **completely untagged** and are notorious for deceptive surface lookalikes. This final checkpoint tests **blind diagnostic recognition** across all five chapters of Part VII (`Ch 26`–`Ch 30`). None of the visible problem statements in Section 2 reveal which chapter or technique applies.

::: {.callout-important title="Zero-Spoiler Protocol & Progressive Hints"}
1. **Strict Zero-Spoiler Rule in Visible Statements**: Every problem statement (`CP-VII-01` through `CP-VII-08`) is written in pure contest form without naming the target chapter (`Ch 26`–`Ch 30`) or technique (`Signed Parallel DSU`, `Chordal Chromatic Product`, `AC-DFA BEST`, `RLBWT Move Structure`, `Centroid Dual-SAM`, `Stack-Trie / SL2(Fp)`, `Thue–Morse Decimation`, or `Morphic KMP Composition`).
2. **Diagnose Before Peeking**: Before opening any dropdown on a problem, write down on scratch paper:
   - Which **Part VII paradigm** (`Ch 26`–`Ch 30`) is triggered by the constraints and algebraic semantics;
   - Which **lookalike decoy paradigm** must be ruled out, and why;
   - The **combinatorial or algebraic word invariant** that collapses the naive $\Omega(N^2)$ or $\Omega(2^K)$ bottleneck.
3. **Four-Stage Progressive Unmasking**:
   - **Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination**: Identifies the governing paradigm and rules out lookalike decoys purely from constraints and operation semantics.
   - **Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant**: States the exact algebraic, graph-theoretic, or morphic identity needed for the reduction.
   - **Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly**: Outlines the state representation, pushdown/composition order, and complexity target.
   - **Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution**: Full proof, boundary pitfall audit (`BP-7-01` through `BP-7-10`), and implementation contract.
:::

## 1. Blind Diagnostic Triage Guide & Part VII Decoy Elimination

Before attempting the eight blind problems below, study the three primary Part VII **Decoy Pairs** and the 5-way diagnostic flowchart.

### 1.1 Decoy Pair A: Signed Palindrome Word Equations (`Ch 26`) vs. Stack-Trie / $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ Cancellation (`Ch 29`)

Both paradigms involve substring mirror symmetries, reversals, or adjacent pair rules on $S[1..N]$ ($N \le 3 \times 10^5$), and both ask whether substrings are equivalent or count valid configurations. Confusing positional reflection with free-group/stack reduction is fatal:

| Diagnostic Dimension | `Ch 26` Paradigm (`T-5A-01` / `T-5A-02`: Signed Binary-Lifting DSU) | `Ch 29` Paradigm (`T-5B-04`: Stack-Trie LCA/LCE & $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ Hashing) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **How Characters Interact** | **Rigid positional index-to-index equality**: $S[l_1..r_1] = S[l_2..r_2]^R$ locks $S[l_1 + t] = S[r_2 - t]$ for every offset $0 \le t \le L - 1$. Characters never disappear or shift indices! | **Elastic adjacent annihilation**: `cc` $\to \varepsilon$ or `()` $\to \varepsilon$ deletes adjacent pairs and pulls outer characters together across arbitrary distances. |
| **Governing Mathematical Object** | **Bipartite equivalence graph / Signed DSU** across $\lceil \log_2 N \rceil$ dyadic layers with edge parity $d \in \{0, 1\}$ and root self-palindrome bit `is_pal[k][r]`. | **Universal Coxeter Group $\Asterisk (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ or Free Group $F_\Sigma$**: reduced prefixes trace a walk on a rooted **Stack-Trie $\mathcal{T}$** where $\operatorname{red}(S[l..r]) \cong u_{l-1} \leadsto \operatorname{LCA} \leadsto u_r$, or multiply $2 \times 2$ matrices in $GL_2/SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$. |
| **Fatal Misdiagnosis** | Using polynomial or $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ hashing to enforce $M$ static equations $S[l_1..r_1] = S[l_2..r_2]^R$ (hashes only test a *known* string; they cannot count connected components of an *unknown* string!). | Using Manacher's algorithm, PAM, or Signed DSU on stack-exterminable arrays (`ababba` reduces to `ab` even though `ababba` is not a palindrome!). |

### 1.2 Decoy Pair B: Inverse Array Chromatic Product (`Ch 27`) vs. De Bruijn / AC-DFA BEST Theorem (`Ch 28`)

Both paradigms ask you to **reconstruct or count how many strings $S \in \Sigma^N$ induce a given structural summary** modulo $10^9 + 7$ or $998244353$:

| Diagnostic Dimension | `Ch 27` Paradigm (`T-3A-06` / `T-5A-03`: Inverse Reconstruction & SA Adjacency) | `Ch 28` Paradigm (`T-5A-04`: De Bruijn & AC-DFA BEST Theorem) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **What Summary Is Prescribed?** | **Positional border, palindrome, or suffix-rank tables**: KMP $\pi[1..N]$, Z-array $Z[1..N]$, Manacher radii, or Suffix Array $\operatorname{SA}[1..N]$. | **Unordered transition / $k$-mer frequency multisets**: how many times each $k$-mer or each Aho–Corasick transition edge $(u, c)$ is traversed across the entire string. |
| **Governing Counting Formula** | **Equality DSU + Chordal Forbidden-Edge Chromatic Product** $\prod_v \max(0, \sigma - \operatorname{deg}_{\text{prev}}(v))$ (plus mandatory forward verification!), or **SA Adjacency** $\binom{N+K-1-D}{N}$. | **Eulerian Arborescence + BEST Theorem**: $\det L_{\text{out}}^{(r)}(G_{\text{act}}) \cdot \prod_u (\operatorname{outdeg}(u) - 1)! \big/ \prod_{u, c} \operatorname{count}(u, c)!$. |
| **Fatal Misdiagnosis** | Trusting local inequality checks $\pi[i] \le \pi[i-1]+1$ without running forward KMP on the reconstructed string (`\pi = [0,1,0,1,1]` trap!), or forgetting sentinel $\operatorname{rk}[N+1]=0$ in SA Adjacency. | Dividing by $\prod_{u, v} A(u, v)!$ instead of $\prod_{u, c} \operatorname{count}(u, c)!$ when two distinct letters $c_1 \ne c_2$ transition between the same pair of AC states $u \to v$! |

### 1.3 Decoy Pair C: $O(1)$ RLBWT Move Structure (`Ch 28`) vs. Morphic Boundary Recurrence & Singular Words (`Ch 30`) at $N \le 10^{18}$

When a problem queries pattern occurrences or factor counts inside a string of length $N \le 10^{18}$, how do you route between `Ch 26`, `Ch 28`, and `Ch 30`?

| Diagnostic Dimension | `Ch 28` Paradigm (`T-5A-05`: Nishimoto–Tabei $O(1)$ RLBWT Move Structure) | `Ch 30` Paradigm (`T-5B-01..03`: Sturmian Singular Words & 3-Regime Morphisms $\varphi^k$) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **How the $10^{18}$ String Is Specified** | Explicitly given as a **Run-Length Encoded Burrows–Wheeler Transform (`RLBWT`)** of $r \le 10^5$ runs $(c_i, L_i)$ representing a cyclic/Wheeler index. | Generated by a **substitution morphism $\varphi^k(S_0)$**, a recursive pivot rule $s_r = s_{r-1} + t_r + s_{r-1}$, a **Sturmian directive / mechanical rotation**, or **Thue–Morse $\mu(\texttt{0})=\texttt{01}$**. |
| **Query Engine** | Split runs so every input LF-interval overlaps $\le 2$ output runs; step backward `m = |P|` times in **strict $O(1)$ time per character** using `(run_id, offset)`. | **3-Regime Morphic Decomposition** ((1) $\|\Sigma\|+\|\Sigma\|^2$ 2-letter junction matrix, (2) $O(\|P\|)$ KMP functional composition for mortal/unit letters, (3) `CF 1466G` level promotion $r_0$), **Zeckendorf / Singular Word ramps**, or **$\mu^{-1}$ parity decimation**. |

## 2. Unspoiled Blind Checkpoint Problems (`CP-VII-01` – `CP-VII-08`)

---

### Problem `CP-VII-01` — Symmetric Mirror Constraint Codes

A communication protocol transmits an unknown string $S[1..N]$ of length $N$ over an alphabet of size $\sigma$, where $1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5$ and $1 \le \sigma \le 10^9$. Before transmission, the protocol enforces $M$ structural constraints ($1 \le M \le 2 \times 10^5$), each of one of two types:

- `1 l1 r1 l2 r2` ($r_1 - l_1 = r_2 - l_2$): The substring $S[l_1..r_1]$ must be **identical** to $S[l_2..r_2]$ ($S[l_1 + t] = S[l_2 + t]$ for all $0 \le t \le r_1 - l_1$).
- `2 l1 r1 l2 r2` ($r_1 - l_1 = r_2 - l_2$): The substring $S[l_1..r_1]$ must be the **exact reversal** of $S[l_2..r_2]$ ($S[l_1 + t] = S[r_2 - t]$ for all $0 \le t \le r_1 - l_1$).

Furthermore, $K$ positions $p_1, \dots, p_K \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ already have their characters fixed to known values $c_1, \dots, c_K \in \{1, \dots, \sigma\}$. Compute the number of valid strings $S[1..N]$ satisfying all $M$ substring constraints and all $K$ point assignments modulo $10^9 + 7$ (outputting `0` if the fixed positions conflict).

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N, M \le 2 \times 10^5$, $0 \le K \le N$, $1 \le \sigma \le 10^9$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: Do not confuse type-2 reversal constraints with stack cancellation (`CP-VII-02`) or PAM `slink` DP: here every constraint locks specific index pairs $S[i] = S[j]$ in an unknown string of length $N$.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Uniting $r_1 - l_1 + 1$ character pairs one by one takes $\Omega(NM)$ time. Because each constraint of length $L = r_1 - l_1 + 1$ can be covered by two overlapping blocks of power-of-two length $2^k$ ($k = \lfloor \log_2 L \rfloor$), we can merge intervals at layer $k$ of a $\lceil \log_2 N \rceil$-layer DSU—provided we track **orientation parity** $d \in \{0, 1\}$ (direct vs. reversed)!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
In a Signed Binary-Lifting DSU where node $(k, i)$ represents the substring $B_k(i) = S[i .. i + 2^k - 1]$:

- A direct equality $S[l_1..r_1] = S[l_2..r_2]$ of length $L$ splits into $B_k(l_1) = B_k(l_2)$ and $B_k(r_1 - 2^k + 1) = B_k(r_2 - 2^k + 1)$ with relative orientation $d = 0$.
- A reversed equality $S[l_1..r_1] = S[l_2..r_2]^R$ maps the **prefix** of $[l_1, r_1]$ to the **reversed suffix** of $[l_2, r_2]$: $B_k(l_1) = B_k(r_2 - 2^k + 1)^R$ and $B_k(r_1 - 2^k + 1) = B_k(l_2)^R$ with relative orientation $d = 1$!
- **Crucial Invariant**: What happens if we unite $(x, y)$ at layer $k$ with orientation $d$, and `find(k, x)` and `find(k, y)` **already share the same DSU root $r$** with net relative orientation $d_x \oplus d_y \oplus d = 1$? Then $B_k(r) = B_k(r)^R$: the root block itself is forced to be a **self-palindrome**, which must be recorded in a boolean flag `is_pal[k][r] = 1`!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Maintain `parent[k][i]`, orientation-to-parent `rel[k][i] \in \{0, 1\}`, and `is_pal[k][i] \in \{0, 1\}` for $0 \le k \le \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$ and $1 \le i \le N - 2^k + 1$.
2. Insert all $M$ constraints at their respective layers $k = \lfloor \log_2 L \rfloor$: when `unite(k, x, y, d)` finds `rx == ry` and `(dx ^ dy ^ d) == 1`, set `is_pal[k][rx] = 1` (and when `rx != ry`, set `is_pal[k][ry] |= is_pal[k][rx]`).
3. Push down from $k = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$ down to $1$:
   - First, for every root $r$ at layer $k$ with `is_pal[k][r] == 1`, call `unite(k - 1, r, r + (1 << (k - 1)), 1)`.
   - Second, for every $i \ne r = \operatorname{find}(k, i)$ with orientation $d = \operatorname{rel}[k][i]$:
     - If $d == 0$: `unite(k - 1, i, r, 0)` and `unite(k - 1, i + (1 << (k - 1)), r + (1 << (k - 1)), 0)`.
     - If $d == 1$: **cross-swap the two halves**: `unite(k - 1, i, r + (1 << (k - 1)), 1)` and `unite(k - 1, i + (1 << (k - 1)), r, 1)`.
4. At layer $k = 0$, check that no component contains two distinct fixed values $c_a \ne c_b$; if $C_{\text{free}}$ components have no fixed position, the answer is $\sigma^{C_{\text{free}}} \bmod (10^9 + 7)$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-VII-01"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 26](../chapters/ch26-word-equations-signed-parallel-dsu.qmd) (`T-5A-01`: Signed Binary-Lifting DSU `倍增并查集` with Root Self-Palindrome Bit `is_pal[k][r]`)**.
- **Why Both Halves Cross-Swap & Why `is_pal[k][r]` Is Mandatory**:
  For a block $B_k(i) = L_i R_i$ of length $2^k$ split into two halves $L_i = B_{k-1}(i)$ and $R_i = B_{k-1}(i + 2^{k-1})$ of length $2^{k-1}$, reversing $B_k(r) = L_r R_r$ produces:
  $$B_k(r)^R = (L_r R_r)^R = R_r^R L_r^R.$$
  Therefore, $B_k(i) = B_k(r)^R$ is equivalent to the two half-length reversed equalities $L_i = R_r^R$ and $R_i = L_r^R$. Furthermore, if two constraints imply both $B_k(x) = B_k(r)$ and $B_k(x) = B_k(r)^R$ (or if a single constraint imposes $S[1..4] = S[1..4]^R$, which splits at $k = 2$ into `unite(2, 1, 1, 1)` where `rx == ry == 1`!), no new edge is added to the spanning forest at layer $k$, yet $B_k(r) = B_k(r)^R$ forces $L_r = R_r^R$ at layer $k - 1$. Storing `is_pal[k][r] = 1` and pushing `unite(k - 1, r, r + 2^{k-1}, 1)` before decomposing non-root nodes captures every self-reflection losslessly!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-7-01`)**:
  - **The $N = 4$ Self-Loop Early-Return Bug**: If `unite(k, x, y, d)` simply returns when `rx == ry` without setting `is_pal[k][rx] |= (dx ^ dy ^ d)`, then on $N = 4$ with constraint `2 1 4 1 4` ($S[1..4] = S[1..4]^R$), `unite(2, 1, 1, 1)` does nothing, leaving $4$ free components ($\sigma^4$) instead of $2$ ($\sigma^2$)!
- **Complexity**: $O\bigl((N \log N + M) \alpha(N)\bigr)$ time and $O(N \log N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-VII-02` — Dynamic Bracket & Pair Annihilation Queries

You are given a string $S[1..N]$ of length $N \le 2 \times 10^5$ over an alphabet of $K \le 10^5$ bracket types: for each type $t \in \{1, \dots, K\}$, there is an opening character $(_t$ and a closing character $)_t$. You must process $Q \le 2 \times 10^5$ operations of two flavors:

- **Subtask A (Dynamic Directed Dyck Validity)**: Support point updates $S[i] \leftarrow c$ and range queries `[l, r]` asking whether $S[l..r]$ is a **valid balanced multi-type Dyck word** (where only an opening bracket $(_t$ on the left and a matching closing bracket $)_t$ on the right may cancel: $(_t )_t \to \varepsilon$, whereas $)_t (_t$ **does not** cancel!).
- **Subtask B (Static Symmetric Reduction Order)**: In a static version where each character $c \in \{1, \dots, K\}$ is self-inverse (`cc` $\to \varepsilon$), answer $Q$ queries `(l1, r1, l2, r2)` comparing the fully stack-reduced forms $\operatorname{red}(S[l_1..r_1])$ and $\operatorname{red}(S[l_2..r_2])$ lexicographically (`<`, `=`, or `>`).

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N, Q, K \le 2 \times 10^5$, Time Limit $2.5\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: Unlike `CP-VII-01`, characters here **annihilate dynamically on a stack**, shifting the relative alignment of all surviving characters!
- **Diagnostic Signal**:
  - In **Subtask A**, point updates invalidate static tries, requiring a Segment Tree of $2 \times 2$ matrices in $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ or reduced stack monoids. Crucially, in $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$, a matrix inverse satisfies $M_t^{-1} M_t = I_2$ just like $M_t M_t^{-1} = I_2$, which would falsely cancel $)_t (_t \to \varepsilon$! Even if you also check that the 1D bracket balance $\operatorname{bal}[k]$ never drops below $\operatorname{bal}[l-1]$, what happens on the multi-type string `([)(])` or `((][))`?
  - In **Subtask B**, $2 \times 2$ matrix hashes cannot compare two reduced strings *lexicographically* without knowing where their first mismatch occurs in the *reduced* string! How do we represent all reduced substrings $\operatorname{red}(S[l..r])$ deterministically as paths on a tree?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
1. **Subtask A (The `((][))` / `([)(])` Trap & Directed Dyck Monoids)**:
   On $S = \texttt{((][))}$ (where an inner `] [` of type $2$ sits inside outer `( (` of type $1$) or $S = \texttt{([)(])}$, the 1D balance array is $[1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 0] \ge 0$ everywhere, yet if closing and opening brackets of type $t$ use $M_t^{-1}$ and $M_t$, then in `((][))` the inner $]_2 [_2$ cancels via $M_2^{-1} M_2 = I_2$ (giving $M_1 M_1 M_2^{-1} M_2 M_1^{-1} M_1^{-1} = I_2$), and in `([)(])` height-indexed involution matrices cancel $[_2$ (up-step $1 \to 2$) with $)_1$ (down-step $2 \to 1$) unless bracket direction is enforced!
   - **Two Exact Fixes to Kill $)_t (_t$ and `([)(])`**:
     - *Method 1 (Segment Tree of Unmatched Stacks $C^{-1} O$ with $O(\log N)$ Binary-Lifting Hash Merge)*: In any segment $[L, R]$ under directed reduction $(_t )_t \to \varepsilon$, the reduced form is a sequence of unmatched closing brackets followed by unmatched opening brackets, $C^{-1} O$. Merging $(C_1^{-1} O_1)$ and $(C_2^{-1} O_2)$ checks whether the shorter of $O_1$ and $C_2$ matches by descending the Segment Tree in $O(\log N)$ steps using polynomial/matrix hashes.
     - *Method 2 (Height-Indexed $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ Generators $M_{(t, d)}$ for Open $(_t$ at $d-1 \to d$ and $M_{(t, d)}^{-1}$ for Close $)_t$ at $d \to d-1$, Paired with Free-Group Prefix-Length Monotonicity)*: A word $W$ reduces to $\varepsilon$ under directed Dyck rules $(_t )_t \to \varepsilon$ if and only if $W = 1$ in the free group $F_\Sigma$ **and** every closing bracket $)_t$ strictly decreases the free-group reduced prefix length (equivalently, no $)_t (_t$ cancellation occurs).
2. **Subtask B (Deterministic Stack-Trie Path Isomorphism)**:
   Walk $i = 1 \dots N$ on a rooted **Stack-Trie $\mathcal{T}$** ($u_0 = \text{root}$; at step $i$, if the edge above $u_{i-1}$ has label $S[i]$, set $u_i = \operatorname{parent}(u_{i-1})$, else step to child $\operatorname{ch}[u_{i-1}][S[i]]$). Then for **every** substring $S[l..r]$, its reduced form $\operatorname{red}(S[l..r]) = P_{l-1}^{-1} P_r$ is **literally the sequence of edge labels along the unique simple tree path $u_{l-1} \leadsto \operatorname{LCA}_{\mathcal{T}}(u_{l-1}, u_r) \leadsto u_r$**!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. **For Subtask B (Static Lexicographical Comparison)**:
   - Build the Stack-Trie $\mathcal{T}$ in $O(N \log K)$ time, along with binary-lifting ancestors `up[j][u]` and upward/downward polynomial tree-path hashes.
   - To compare $\operatorname{red}(S[l_1..r_1])$ (path $u_{l_1-1} \leadsto w_1 \leadsto u_{r_1}$) and $\operatorname{red}(S[l_2..r_2])$ (path $u_{l_2-1} \leadsto w_2 \leadsto u_{r_2}$), binary-lift the Longest Common Extension ($\operatorname{LCE}$) along the two tree paths in $O(\log N)$ time, then compare the very next edge label!
2. **For Subtask A (Dynamic Point-Update Directed Dyck)**:
   - How do we prevent $)_t (_t \to I_2$ in a Segment Tree under point updates?
   - In any segment $[L, R]$, if we only allow $(_t )_t \to \varepsilon$ (and **never** $)_t (_t \to \varepsilon$), any substring reduces to a sequence of unmatched closing brackets followed by unmatched opening brackets: $C^{-1} O$. Two adjacent segments $(C_1^{-1} O_1)$ and $(C_2^{-1} O_2)$ merge in the **Bicyclic / Polycyclic Monoid** by canceling the shorter of $O_1$ and $C_2$! Even simpler with $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$: if we maintain the 1D bracket balance array $\operatorname{bal}[i]$ (under point updates, a prefix add in a Fenwick/Segment tree, or when swaps preserve balance) with height-indexed generators $M_{(t, d)}$, or in a Segment Tree where each node stores its net $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ product $M$ **plus** for $O(\log^2 N)$ binary-lifting hash on the unmatched open/close chains (just like Segment Tree Range LCE!), each merge checks if the shorter of $O_1$ and $C_2$ matches in $O(\log N)$ time!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-VII-02"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 29](../chapters/ch29-tree-strings-stack-trie-sl2-hashing.qmd) (`T-5B-04`: Deterministic Stack-Trie Path Isomorphism, Tree-Path LCE & Non-Abelian $GL_2/SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ / Height-Indexed Dyck Hashing)**.
- **Proof of Stack-Trie Path Isomorphism (Subtask B)**:
  Let $P_i = \operatorname{red}(S[1..i])$ be the unique reduced word of prefix $S[1..i]$ in the universal Coxeter group $G_{\text{stack}} = \langle \Sigma \mid c^2 = 1 \rangle$. Each node $u_i$ in the Stack-Trie $\mathcal{T}$ has root-to-$u_i$ path string equal to $P_i$. In $G_{\text{stack}}$, the longest common prefix of $P_{l-1}$ and $P_r$ is the root-to-$w$ path where $w = \operatorname{LCA}_{\mathcal{T}}(u_{l-1}, u_r)$. Writing $P_{l-1} = W A$ and $P_r = W B$ where $A$ and $B$ start with distinct characters (or one is empty), we have:
  $$\operatorname{red}(S[l..r]) = P_{l-1}^{-1} P_r = (W A)^{-1} (W B) = A^{-1} W^{-1} W B = A^R B.$$
  Since $A^R$ is the sequence of edge labels walking **upward** from $u_{l-1}$ to $w$, and $B$ is the sequence of edge labels walking **downward** from $w$ to $u_r$, and the first edges of $A$ and $B$ out of $w$ are distinct, no further cancellation can occur at $w$! Thus $\operatorname{red}(S[l..r])$ is **100% isomorphic to the simple tree path $u_{l-1} \leadsto w \leadsto u_r$**. Binary lifting with upward and downward tree hashes finds the exact $\operatorname{LCE}$ of two reduced substrings in $O(\log N)$ time with **zero matrices**.
- **Directed Dyck Resolution & Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-7-02`)**:
  - **The Un-Indexed $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ Counterexample `(( ] [ ))`**: On $S = \texttt{((][))}$, the 1D balance array is $[1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 0] \ge 0$, and the un-indexed $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ product is $M_1 M_1 M_2^{-1} M_2 M_1^{-1} M_1^{-1} = I_2$, falsely reporting a valid Dyck word!
  - **The Exact Segment-Tree Resolution**: An opening bracket $(_t$ at index $i$ must match a closing bracket **to its right**, whereas $)_t (_t$ has closing on the left! In a Segment Tree, each node $[L, R]$ maintains its reduced form $C^{-1} O$ (a hash of unmatched closing brackets $C$ and unmatched opening brackets $O$): when merging Left $(C_1, O_1)$ and Right $(C_2, O_2)$, if $|O_1| \ge |C_2|$, we check in $O(\log N)$ down the Segment Tree whether the suffix of $O_1$ of length $|C_2|$ equals $C_2$, and combine the remaining unmatched parts! That Segment-Tree Range-Stack merge runs in $O(\log^2 N)$ time per point update and range query, completely immune to `(( ] [ ))` and `([)(])`!
- **Complexity**: $O(N \log K + Q \log N)$ for Subtask B; $O(Q \log^2 N)$ for full point-update multi-type Dyck in Subtask A.
::::

### Problem `CP-VII-03` — Consistent Border & Radius Witness Synthesis

An unknown string $S[1..N]$ of length $N \le 2 \times 10^5$ over an alphabet $\Sigma = \{0, 1, \dots, \sigma - 1\}$ ($\sigma \le 10^9$) was processed by a string analyzer, which recorded its longest proper border array $\pi[1..N]$ (where $\pi[i]$ is the length of the longest proper prefix of $S[1..i]$ that is also a suffix of $S[1..i]$) and its odd-length palindrome radius array $R[1..N]$ (where $R[i] \ge 1$ is the largest integer such that $S[i - R[i] + 1 .. i + R[i] - 1]$ is a palindrome).

Given the arrays $\pi[1..N]$ and $R[1..N]$:

1. Determine whether there exists at least one valid string $S \in \Sigma^N$ whose longest proper border array is **exactly** $\pi[1..N]$ and whose odd-length palindrome radius array is **exactly** $R[1..N]$.
2. If valid strings exist, output the **lexicographically smallest** valid string $S_{\min}$, and compute the **total number of valid strings** $S \in \Sigma^N$ modulo $10^9 + 7$.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5$, $1 \le \sigma \le 10^9$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: We are given positional border/palindrome tables $\pi[1..N]$ and $R[1..N]$, *not* De Bruijn edge counts (`CP-VII-04`).
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Every KMP entry $\pi[i]$ and Manacher entry $R[i]$ imposes two kinds of constraints on $S$:
  1. **Forced Character Equalities ($=$)**: $S[1..\pi[i]] = S[i-\pi[i]+1..i]$ (specifically $S[\pi[i]] = S[i]$ when $\pi[1..i-1]$ already holds) and $S[i-R[i]+1..i+R[i]-1] = S[i-R[i]+1..i+R[i]-1]^R$.
  2. **Forbidden Character Mismatches ($\ne$)**: For every border $b$ on the KMP fail chain of $i-1$ that fails to extend at step $i$ ($b + 1 > \pi[i]$), we must have $S[b + 1] \ne S[i]$; and if $i - R[i] \ge 1$ and $i + R[i] \le N$, the palindrome expansion stopped because $S[i - R[i]] \ne S[i + R[i]]$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
1. **Uniting Equalities in $O(N \log N)$**: Use a Binary-Lifting Parallel DSU (`Ch 26`) to merge all palindrome intervals $S[i-R[i]+1..i] = S[i..i+R[i]-1]^R$ and KMP border equalities $S[\pi[i]] = S[i]$ into connected components!
2. **Why Chromatic Counting Is Easy Only When the Graph Is Chordal / Acyclic**:
   For KMP + Z-array + Manacher, every mismatch $S[i] \ne S[j]$ ($j < i$) at the first occurrence of a DSU component links $i$ to a set of earlier DSU components that already pairwise disagree with each other (forming a **clique** of previous components!), making the inequality graph on DSU components **chordal**!
   Here, verify that after contracting the equality DSU components (and checking that no forbidden edge $u \ne v$ has $\operatorname{find}(u) == \operatorname{find}(v)$), we can greedily assign each component $C$ (ordered by its minimum index $\min C$) the smallest available character $c \notin \{\text{colors of earlier forbidden neighbors}\}$, and then **run a mandatory forward KMP and Manacher pass on $S_{\min}$** to verify that $\pi(S_{\min}) = \pi$ and $R(S_{\min}) = R$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Check basic range bounds ($\pi[1] = 0$, $\pi[i] \le \pi[i-1] + 1$, $1 \le R[i] \le \min(i, N - i + 1)$).
2. In a Signed Binary-Lifting DSU of depth $\lceil \log_2 N \rceil$, unite $S[\pi[i]] = S[i]$ (if $\pi[i] > 0$) and $S[i-R[i]+1..i] = S[i..i+R[i]-1]^R$ for all $i$. Push down to layer $0$.
3. Collect all forbidden edges $(u, v)$:
   - From KMP at step $i$: walk $b = \pi[i-1]$ down the $\pi$-chain until $b + 1 = \pi[i]$ (using `anc` or direct walk since each border dies at most once if $\pi$ is valid!), adding forbidden edge $(b + 1, i)$.
   - From Manacher at center $i$: if $i - R[i] \ge 1$ and $i + R[i] \le N$, add forbidden edge $(i - R[i], i + R[i])$.
4. Contract forbidden edges to layer-0 DSU roots. If any edge is a self-loop, return `0` / impossible. Order components by their earliest index $first[r]$: assign $S_{\min}[r] = \operatorname{mex}\{S_{\min}[u] : (u, r) \in E_{\ne}, first[u] < first[r]\}$.
5. **Mandatory Forward Verification (`BP-7-03`)**: Run standard $O(N)$ KMP and $O(N)$ Manacher on $S_{\min}$! If the resulting arrays do not equal $\pi[1..N]$ and $R[1..N]$ (or if any component needed a character $\ge \sigma$), output `0`. Otherwise, when the forbidden predecessors of each component $r$ are forced to have pairwise distinct colors ( forming a clique of size $d_{\text{prev}}(r)$), the total count is $\prod_r (\sigma - d_{\text{prev}}(r)) \bmod (10^9 + 7)$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-VII-03"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 27](../chapters/ch27-inverse-reconstruction-inequality-dags.qmd) (`T-3A-06`: Inverse String Reconstruction via Equality DSU, Chordal Forbidden-Edge Chromatic Product & Mandatory Forward Verification)**.
- **Why Forward Verification Is Non-Negotiable (`BP-7-03`)**:
  Consider $\pi = [0, 1, 0, 1, 1]$ ($N = 5$) with trivial $R = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1]$. Notice that $\pi[i] \le \pi[i-1] + 1$ holds at every index! The positive equalities force $S[1] = S[2] = S[4] = S[5]$, and the mismatch at $i = 3$ forces $S[3] \ne S[2] = S[1]$. Thus for $\sigma = 2$, the *only* candidate up to relabeling is $S = \texttt{aabaa}$. Yet running forward KMP on $\texttt{aabaa}$ produces $\pi(\texttt{aabaa}) = [0, 1, 0, 1, \mathbf{2}] \ne [0, 1, 0, 1, 1]$ (and $R(\texttt{aabaa})[3] = 3 \ne 1$)! Why? Because at $i = 5$, walking $\pi[4] = 1$ tests $S[\pi[4] + 1] = S[2]$ against $S[5]$—requiring $S[2] \ne S[5]$ so $\pi[5]$ does not become $2$, which contradicts $S[2] = S[1] = S[5]$! Forward verification catches every hidden contradiction in $O(N)$ time.
- **Why the Forbidden Predecessor Set Forms a Clique**:
  At step $r$ (the first occurrence of a DSU component), every forbidden neighbor $u$ with $first[u] < first[r]$ arises from failing to extend a border or palindrome that already matched up to $r - 1$. If two such forbidden positions $u_1, u_2$ had the same character $S[u_1] = S[u_2]$, then by symmetry across the matched prefix/palindrome before $r$, $u_1$ and $u_2$ would already be in the **same DSU component** (or one border would have extended the other!). Thus the set of distinct earlier DSU components adjacent to $r$ in $E_{\ne}$ must receive **pairwise distinct characters** in every valid string, making the number of choices for component $r$ equal to $\max(0, \sigma - d_{\text{prev}}(r))$ independent of which valid characters were chosen for earlier components!
- **Complexity**: $O(N \log N \cdot \alpha(N))$ time and $O(N \log N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-VII-04` — Prescribed Automaton Transition Telemetry

A network monitor builds the minimal prefix-tree deterministic finite automaton (DFA) $\mathcal{A}$ (where every state $u$ corresponds to a prefix of some dictionary pattern, and reading character $c$ transitions to the state $\delta(u, c)$ representing the longest suffix of $\operatorname{str}(u) + c$ that is a prefix of some dictionary pattern) over alphabet $\Sigma = \{\texttt{'a'}, \dots, \texttt{'z'}\}$ from a dictionary of $K$ pattern strings $P_1, \dots, P_K$ ($\sum |P_i| \le 300$). When a packet string $S[1..N]$ is fed into $\mathcal{A}$ starting at the root state $u_0 = 0$, it traces a sequence of $N$ transitions:
$$u_{i-1} \xrightarrow{S[i]} u_i = \delta(u_{i-1},\; S[i]) \qquad (1 \le i \le N).$$
You are given the dictionary $P_1, \dots, P_K$ and a telemetry matrix $C[u][c] \ge 0$ ($0 \le u < V, c \in \Sigma$) specifying the **exact number of times** the transition from state $u$ on character $c$ was traversed, with $\sum_{u, c} C[u][c] = N \le 10^7$. Count the number of distinct strings $S \in \Sigma^N$ that start at $u_0 = 0$ and induce the exact transition counts $C[u][c]$ modulo $998244353$.

- **Constraints**: $V \le 301$, $|\Sigma| \le 26$, $N = \sum C[u][c] \le 10^7$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: Unlike `CP-VII-03` (which prescribes positional border tables), here we are given the **multiset of directed transitions $(u, c)$** traversed in the Aho–Corasick DFA $\mathcal{A}$.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Because the DFA transition function $\delta(u, c)$ is deterministic, a sequence of characters $S[1..N]$ starting at $u_0 = 0$ induces the transition counts $C[u][c]$ **if and only if** it corresponds to an **Eulerian walk** starting at $u_0 = 0$ in the directed multigraph $G$ where each pair $(u, c)$ contributes $C[u][c]$ directed edges $u \xrightarrow{c} \delta(u, c)$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Let $\operatorname{outdeg}(u) = \sum_{c \in \Sigma} C[u][c]$ and $\operatorname{indeg}(v) = \sum_{u, c : \delta(u, c) = v} C[u][c]$.

1. **Degree & Connectedness Feasibility**: A valid walk starting at $u_0 = 0$ and ending at some unique terminal state $v_{\text{end}}$ exists iff either $\operatorname{outdeg}(u) = \operatorname{indeg}(u)$ for all $u$ (so $v_{\text{end}} = u_0 = 0$), or $\operatorname{outdeg}(u_0) - \operatorname{indeg}(u_0) = 1$, $\operatorname{indeg}(v_{\text{end}}) - \operatorname{outdeg}(v_{\text{end}}) = 1$, and $\operatorname{outdeg}(u) = \operatorname{indeg}(u)$ for all other $u$—and all vertices with $\operatorname{outdeg}(u) > 0$ are reachable from $u_0 = 0$!
2. **The AC-DFA BEST Theorem & The Parallel-Edge Trap (`BP-7-04`)**:
   By the **BEST (de Bruijn–van Aardenne-Ehrenfest–Smith–Tutte) Theorem**, the number of edge-labeled Eulerian walks from $u_0$ to $v_{\text{end}}$ (adding 1 virtual return edge $v_{\text{end}} \to u_0$ if $v_{\text{end}} \ne u_0$) is:
   $$\det L_{\text{out}}^{(v_{\text{end}})}(G_{\text{act}}) \cdot \prod_{u \in V_{\text{act}}} \bigl(\operatorname{outdeg}^+(u) - 1\bigr)! \quad \text{(counting all } C[u][c] \text{ edges as distinct)}.$$
   Now, how do we convert from distinct edge-orderings to distinct **strings** $S \in \Sigma^N$?
   - All $C[u][c]$ copies of the transition $u \xrightarrow{c} \delta(u, c)$ carry the **same character $c$**, so permuting them among themselves produces the **exact same string** $S$: we must divide by $C[u][c]!$.
   - **Warning (`UOJ #607` Parallel-Edge Trap)**: What if two **different** characters $c_1 \ne c_2$ from the same state $u$ transition to the **same target state** $v = \delta(u, c_1) = \delta(u, c_2)$ (for example, both failing back to $v = 0$)? Those edges carry **different characters $c_1 \ne c_2$**, so swapping them produces **distinct strings**! Therefore, we must divide by $\prod_{u, c} C[u][c]!$, **NEVER** by $\prod_{u, v} A(u, v)!$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Build the AC DFA $\delta(u, c)$ in $O(V |\Sigma|)$ time.
2. Compute $\operatorname{outdeg}(u)$ and $\operatorname{indeg}(u)$ from $C[u][c]$. Identify $v_{\text{end}}$ (or return `0` if degrees or reachability from $u_0 = 0$ fail; handle $N = 0 \implies 1$ separately).
3. Restrict to the active vertex set $V_{\text{act}} = \{u : \operatorname{outdeg}(u) + \operatorname{indeg}(u) > 0\}$. Check that $u_0 \in V_{\text{act}}$ and every $u \in V_{\text{act}}$ can reach $v_{\text{end}}$ (equivalently is reachable from $u_0$).
4. Form the out-degree Laplacian $L_{\text{out}}$ on $V_{\text{act}}$: $L_{u, u} = \sum_{v \ne u} A(u, v)$ and $L_{u, v} = -A(u, v)$ where $A(u, v) = \sum_{c : \delta(u, c) = v} C[u][c]$ (note: self-loops $u \to u$ cancel on the diagonal of $L_{\text{out}}$, though they ARE included in $\operatorname{outdeg}(u)$ for the factorial $(\operatorname{outdeg}(u) - 1)!$!).
5. Compute the cofactor $\det L_{\text{out}}^{(v_{\text{end}})}$ by $O(|V_{\text{act}}|^3)$ Gaussian elimination modulo $998244353$, and multiply by:
   $$\frac{\operatorname{outdeg}(v_{\text{end}})! \cdot \prod_{u \in V_{\text{act}} \setminus \{v_{\text{end}}\}} (\operatorname{outdeg}(u) - 1)!}{\prod_{u \in V_{\text{act}}} \prod_{c \in \Sigma} C[u][c]!} \pmod{998244353}.$$
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-VII-04"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 28](../chapters/ch28-debruijn-best-bwt-wheeler-rlbwt.qmd) (`T-5A-04`: Aho–Corasick DFA Eulerian Bijection, BEST Theorem & Parallel-Edge Indistinguishability Invariant · `UOJ #607` Archetype)**.
- **Proof of the Exact AC-DFA BEST Formula**:
  In the directed multigraph $G$ with $C[u][c]$ edges labeled $(u, c) \to \delta(u, c)$, adding one auxiliary reference edge $e^* : v_{\text{end}} \to u_0$ creates a balanced Eulerian multigraph $G^+$ where $\operatorname{outdeg}^+(v_{\text{end}}) = \operatorname{outdeg}(v_{\text{end}}) + 1$ and $\operatorname{outdeg}^+(u) = \operatorname{outdeg}(u)$ for $u \ne v_{\text{end}}$. By the BEST Theorem, there is a bijection between Eulerian circuits of $G^+$ starting with $e^*$ (i.e., Eulerian walks of $G$ from $u_0$ to $v_{\text{end}}$) and pairs consisting of:
  1. An **oriented spanning arborescence** $\mathcal{T}$ of $G_{\text{act}}$ rooted at $v_{\text{end}}$ (counted by Tutte's Directed Matrix-Tree Theorem as $\det L_{\text{out}}^{(v_{\text{end}})}(G_{\text{act}})$, where self-loops do not belong to any arborescence and thus cancel from $L_{\text{out}}$, while still contributing to the cyclic ordering of outgoing edges at each vertex!), and
  2. For each vertex $u \in V_{\text{act}}$, a linear ordering of its $\operatorname{outdeg}^+(u) - 1$ non-arborescence outgoing edges (including self-loops!), giving $(\operatorname{outdeg}^+(u) - 1)!$ ways.
  Since two Eulerian walks of $G$ produce the **exact same string** $S[1..N]$ iff at every step $i$ they traverse edges with the same character $S[i] = c_i$ (which by determinism of $\delta(u_0, S[1..i])$ means they visit the exact same state sequence $u_0, u_1, \dots, u_N$ and differ only by permuting the $C[u][c]$ identical copies of $(u, c)$), each distinct string $S$ corresponds to **exactly $\prod_{u, c} C[u][c]!$** edge-distinct Eulerian walks!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-7-04`, `BP-7-05`)**:
  - **Pitfall 1 (`BP-7-04` — The Parallel-Edge Trap)**: Dividing by $\prod_{u, v} A(u, v)!$ instead of $\prod_{u, c} C[u][c]!$ fails whenever two different characters $c_1 \ne c_2$ transition between the same states $u \to v$.
  - **Pitfall 2 (`BP-7-05` — Self-Loops in $L_{\text{out}}$ vs. $(\operatorname{outdeg}(u) - 1)!$)**: Self-loops $u \xrightarrow{c} u$ (such as reading a non-pattern letter at the AC root $0 \to 0$) contribute $0$ to the Laplacian matrix $L_{\text{out}}$ (since $L_{u,u}$ sums $A(u, v)$ only for $v \ne u$), but they **must** be included in $\operatorname{outdeg}(u)$ inside the factorial $(\operatorname{outdeg}^+(u) - 1)!$!
- **Complexity**: $O(V^3 + V|\Sigma| + N)$ time and $O(V^2 + V|\Sigma| + N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-VII-05` — All-Pairs Tree-Walk Pattern Census

You are given an unrooted tree $T$ with $N$ vertices ($1 \le N \le 5 \times 10^4$), where each vertex $u$ is labeled with a character $C[u] \in \{\texttt{'a'}, \dots, \texttt{'z'}\}$, and a reference string $P[1..M]$ ($1 \le M \le 5 \times 10^4$). For any ordered pair of vertices $(u, v)$ ($1 \le u, v \le N$), let $\operatorname{str}(u \leadsto v)$ be the string formed by concatenating the vertex characters along the unique simple path from $u$ to $v$.

Compute the sum, over all $N^2$ ordered pairs $(u, v)$, of the number of times $\operatorname{str}(u \leadsto v)$ occurs as a contiguous substring inside $P[1..M]$:
$$\sum_{u=1}^N \sum_{v=1}^N \operatorname{occ}\bigl(\operatorname{str}(u \leadsto v),\; P[1..M]\bigr).$$

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N, M \le 5 \times 10^4$, Time Limit $3.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: The tree can have up to $N - 1$ leaves (star graph), so the 20-Leaf Generalized SAM trick (`[ZJOI2015]`) is impossible here!
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Counting paths on an arbitrary tree splits naturally via **Centroid Decomposition**! At a centroid $r$ of a component of size $S_c$, every simple path $u \leadsto v$ passing through $r$ decomposes at $r$ into an upward prefix $u \leadsto r$ and a downward suffix $r \leadsto v$, splitting the match against $P[1..M]$ at the midpoint character $P[i] = C[r]$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Build $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$ and $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$:

- Walking downward from $r$ to $v$ in $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$ tracks whether $\operatorname{str}(r \leadsto v)$ occurs in $P$; walking downward from $r$ to $u$ in $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$ tracks whether $\operatorname{str}(u \leadsto r) = \operatorname{str}(r \leadsto u)^R$ occurs in $P$!
- **Why Naive Centroid Decomposition Still TLEs on Star Subtrees**: To count paths $u \leadsto r \leadsto v$ matching inside $P$, we can propagate path counts down the Link Trees of $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$ and $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$ in $O(M)$ time and dot-product matching midpoint positions $i \in [1, M]$. **However**:
  1. If $S_c < \sqrt{M}$, an $O(M)$ Link-Tree sweep at every small centroid component takes $O(N M)$ total time!
  2. Even when $S_c > \sqrt{M}$, subtracting same-child-subtree pairs $(u, v) \in T_{\text{sub}} \times T_{\text{sub}}$ by running an $O(M)$ Link-Tree sweep per child subtree also TLEs when $r$ has $\Theta(\sqrt{M})$ children!
  - **The Dual $\sqrt{M}$ Split (`[CTSC2010] 珠宝商`)**: Threshold **both** the centroid component size $S_c$ AND each individual child subtree size $|T_{\text{sub}}|$ against $B = \sqrt{M}$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
Fix threshold $B = \lfloor \sqrt{M} \rfloor \approx 220$:

1. **Light Component or Light Child Subtree ($\text{size} \le B$)**: There are at most $\text{size}^2$ pairs $(u, v)$! Simply run a direct DFS from each node $u$ in the light component (or inside the light child subtree $T_{\text{sub}}$ to subtract same-subtree pairs), stepping through $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$ in $O(1)$ per edge and adding $\operatorname{cnt}_{\text{SAM}(P)}(\text{state})$ in $O(\text{size}^2) \le O(\text{size} \cdot B)$ time!
2. **Heavy Component ($S_c > B$) & Heavy Child Subtrees ($|T_{\text{sub}}| > B$)**:
   - Notice that to step $u \leadsto r$ *upward* while walking *downward* from $r$ to $u$, extending the path at the bottom ($u$) **prepends** a character to $\operatorname{str}(u \leadsto r)$, which corresponds to stepping down a **Suffix Tree edge** (i.e., the Link Tree of $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$ or $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$ by checking the character at depth $\text{len}$)!
   - Even simpler: walking downward from $r$ to $v$ builds $\operatorname{str}(r \leadsto v)$ by **appending** characters in $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$, and builds $\operatorname{str}(r \leadsto u) = \operatorname{str}(u \leadsto r)^R$ by **appending** characters in $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$!
   - Accumulate node visits in $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$ and $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$, push counts down both Link Trees to the $M$ prefix positions $i \in [1, M]$, and sum $\operatorname{ways}_{P^R}[M - i + 1] \times \operatorname{ways}_P[i]$ in $O(S_c + M)$ time! Since at most $(N + \sum S_c) / B = O(N \log N / \sqrt{M})$ heavy sweeps ever occur, total time is $O((N \log N / \sqrt{M}) M + N \sqrt{M}) = O(N \sqrt{M \log N})$!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-VII-05"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 29](../chapters/ch29-tree-strings-stack-trie-sl2-hashing.qmd) (`T-5A-06`: Centroid Decomposition + Dual-Threshold $\sqrt{M}$ Heavy-Light SAM Split · `[CTSC2010] 珠宝商` / `Luogu P4218`)**.
- **Exact Midpoint Decomposition on $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$ and $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$**:
  Every occurrence of $\operatorname{str}(u \leadsto r \leadsto v)$ inside $P[1..M]$ aligns the centroid vertex $r$ with a unique index $i \in \{1, \dots, M\}$ such that:
  1. $P[i - \operatorname{dist}(u, r) .. i] = \operatorname{str}(u \leadsto r) \iff P^R[M - i + 1 .. M - i + 1 + \operatorname{dist}(u, r)] = \operatorname{str}(r \leadsto u)$, which holds iff the $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$ state reached by $\operatorname{str}(u \leadsto r)$ is a **Link-Tree ancestor** of the prefix state $\operatorname{pref}_P(i)$ (representing substrings of $P$ ending at index $i$); and
  2. $P[i .. i + \operatorname{dist}(r, v)] = \operatorname{str}(r \leadsto v) \iff P^R[1 .. M - i + 1]$ has suffix $\operatorname{str}(r \leadsto v)^R$, which holds iff the $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$ state reached by $\operatorname{str}(r \leadsto v)^R$ is a **Link-Tree ancestor** of $\operatorname{pref}_{P^R}(M - i + 1)$ (representing substrings of $P$ starting at index $i$)!
  - Walking downward from $r$ to $v$ appends characters to $\operatorname{str}(r \leadsto v)$ (which is a forward walk on $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$ and a Suffix-Tree / Link-Tree child step on $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$), while walking downward from $r$ to $u$ appends characters to $\operatorname{str}(r \leadsto u) = \operatorname{str}(u \leadsto r)^R$ (which is a forward walk on $\operatorname{SAM}(P^R)$ and a Suffix-Tree / Link-Tree child step on $\operatorname{SAM}(P)$). Accumulating state counts and pushing them down the two Link Trees matches all split positions $i \in [1, M]$ in $O(S_c + M)$ time!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-7-06`)**:
  - **Omitting the $\sqrt{M}$ Check on Child Subtrees**: If a centroid $r$ has $S_c = 5 \times 10^4$ split into $200$ child subtrees of size $250$, running an $O(M)$ Link-Tree pass to subtract same-subtree pairs on each of the $200$ children costs $200 \times 5 \times 10^4 = 10^7$ ops per centroid! Applying the $O(|T_{\text{sub}}|^2)$ brute-force subtraction whenever $|T_{\text{sub}}| \le \sqrt{M}$ and the $O(M)$ Link-Tree subtraction only when $|T_{\text{sub}}| > \sqrt{M}$ bounds total work strictly by $O((N + M)\sqrt{M \log N})$.
- **Complexity**: $O\bigl((N + M)\sqrt{M}\bigr)$ time and $O(N + M)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-VII-06` — Run-Compressed Cyclic Index Search at $N \le 10^{18}$

A genomic archive stores a circular text $T[1..N]$ of length $N \le 10^{18}$ (terminated by a unique sentinel `'$'` smaller than all alphabet letters) solely via the **run-length encoding of the last column $L[1..N]$ of its sorted cyclic rotations**, which consists of $r \le 10^5$ runs:
$$L_{\text{RLE}}(T) = \bigl((c_1, L_1),\; (c_2, L_2),\; \dots,\; (c_r, L_r)\bigr), \qquad \sum_{i=1}^r L_i = N \le 10^{18}.$$
You are given the $r$ runs of $L_{\text{RLE}}(T)$ and $Q \le 10^5$ query patterns $P_1, \dots, P_Q$ with $\sum |P_q| \le 5 \times 10^5$. For each query pattern $P$, compute the exact number of occurrences of $P$ in $T$. Your query phase must run in **strict $O(|P|)$ time per query** without binary searching over the $r$ runs at every character step.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le r \le 10^5$, $N \le 10^{18}$, $\sum |P_q| \le 5 \times 10^5$, $|\Sigma| \le 26$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: The string $T$ is **not** generated by a morphism or Fibonacci rule (`CP-VII-07`, `CP-VII-08`); we are given its exact BWT compressed into $r$ equal-letter runs.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Standard FM-index backward search updates the Suffix Array interval $[sp, ep]$ by finding the first and last occurrence of character $c = P[j]$ inside $\operatorname{BWT}[sp..ep]$ and applying the LF-mapping $\operatorname{LF}(i) = C[c] + \operatorname{rank}_c(i)$. If we represent positions as `(run_id, offset)` and use `std::lower_bound` on the $r$ runs at each step, queries take $O(\sum |P_q| \log r)$ time. How did Nishimoto and Tabei (2021) eliminate the $\log r$ binary search to achieve **strict $O(1)$ time per LF-step** in $O(r)$ space?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
1. **Why Raw RLBWT Pointer-Chasing Can Cascade**: Suppose we store for each BWT run $i$ the output run $\operatorname{target}(i)$ containing $\operatorname{LF}(\text{start}_i)$. When an interval boundary moves via $\operatorname{LF}$ to `(target(i), new_offset)`, we might also need to advance across multiple short consecutive runs to find the next run with character $c'$—or if a single input run's $\operatorname{LF}$-image spans $k$ distinct output runs in the $F$-column, computing which output run contains `start_i + offset` requires either binary search or walking $k$ output runs!
2. **The Nishimoto–Tabei Run-Splitting Invariant (`Theorem 28.6`)**:
   Because $\operatorname{LF}$ is strictly order-preserving on every monochromatic run $(c_i, L_i)$, the image $\operatorname{LF}([s_i, e_i])$ is a **single contiguous interval** in the $F$-column! If we split runs so that the $\operatorname{LF}$-image of every run overlaps **at most $2$ runs** (i.e., crosses at most $1$ run boundary in the BWT), then locating the output run of `s_i + offset` requires **at most $1$ pointer step (`if offset >= threshold then ++run_id`)** in $O(1)$ worst-case time, while increasing the total number of runs by at most a factor of $2$ ($\le 2r$)!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Compute prefix sums $s_i = 1 + \sum_{k < i} L_k$ in the $L$-column (BWT) and global character offsets $C[c]$ in the $F$-column, plus the exact $\operatorname{LF}$-image interval $[f_i, f_i + L_i - 1]$ for each run $i$.
2. Split any run whose $\operatorname{LF}$-image crosses $\ge 2$ run boundaries (or build the $2r$ joint boundary subdivisions of $L$-runs and $\operatorname{LF}^{-1}$-images of $L$-run boundaries) so every refined run $i$ maps into at most $2$ refined runs $(\operatorname{out}_i, \operatorname{out}_i + 1)$ with split threshold $\Delta_i$.
3. For each refined run $i$ and each alphabet character $c \in \Sigma$ ($|\Sigma| \le 26$), precompute `next_run[i][c]` (first run $\ge i$ with character $c$) and `prev_run[i][c]` (last run $\le i$ with character $c$) in $O(r |\Sigma|)$ time!
4. To backward-step interval $\bigl[(u_L, d_L),\, (u_R, d_R)\bigr]$ on character $c$:
   - Jump $(u_L, d_L)$ to the first occurrence of $c$: if $c_{u_L} \ne c$, set $(u_L, d_L) \leftarrow (\operatorname{next\_run}[u_L][c], 0)$.
   - Jump $(u_R, d_R)$ to the last occurrence of $c$: if $c_{u_R} \ne c$, set $(u_R, d_R) \leftarrow (\operatorname{prev\_run}[u_R][c], L_{\operatorname{prev}} - 1)$.
   - If the interval is now empty, return `0`; otherwise apply the $O(1)$ Move step to both endpoints!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-VII-06"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 28](../chapters/ch28-debruijn-best-bwt-wheeler-rlbwt.qmd) (`T-5A-05`: Nishimoto–Tabei $O(1)$ RLBWT Move Structure for $N \le 10^{18}$)**.
- **Why Joint Boundary Subdivision Has $\le 2r$ Runs and $O(1)$ Move Time**:
  Place the $r$ run-start positions of the $L$-column onto $[1, N]$, and also map the $r$ run-start positions of the $L$-column backward via $\operatorname{LF}^{-1}$ (or simply intersect the $r$ intervals $\operatorname{LF}(I_k)$ with the $r$ intervals $I_j$). Merging the two sorted lists of $r$ boundary points partitions $[1, N]$ into $r' \le 2r$ refined monochromatic runs! By construction, for every refined run $i \in \{1, \dots, r'\}$, its image $\operatorname{LF}(I_i)$ never contains a run boundary of the original $L$-runs inside its interior, and crosses at most a constant number of refined boundaries—so `move(u, d)` updates `(u, d)` to its exact $\operatorname{LF}$ image `(u', d')` in $O(1)$ pointer comparisons! Paired with `next_run[i][c]` and `prev_run[i][c]` ($|\Sigma| \le 26$), every backward search step runs in **strict $O(1)$ time**!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-7-07`)**:
  - **64-Bit Overflow on Offset Arithmetic**: Since $N \le 10^{18}$, all run lengths $L_i$, character buckets $C[c]$, and internal offsets $d \in [0, L_i - 1]$ must use `long long` (`int64_t`).
- **Complexity**: $O(r |\Sigma|)$ preprocessing time and space; $O(|P|)$ query time per pattern.
::::

### Problem `CP-VII-07` — Parity-Locked Infinite Binary Word Extensions

Consider the infinite binary sequence $\mathbf{w} = w_0 w_1 w_2 \dots \in \{\texttt{'0'}, \texttt{'1'}\}^\omega$ defined by:
$$w_0 = \texttt{'0'}, \qquad w_{2n} = w_n, \qquad w_{2n+1} = \texttt{'1'} - w_n + \texttt{'0'} \quad (n \ge 0).$$
You are given $T \le 100$ testcases. Each testcase gives a binary string $S[1..m]$ ($1 \le m \le 100$) and a non-negative integer $K$ ($0 \le K \le 10^{18}$). Count the number of distinct binary strings $W \in \{\texttt{'0'}, \texttt{'1'}\}^K$ of length $K$ such that the concatenation $S + W$ (of length $m + K$) occurs at least once as a contiguous substring of $\mathbf{w}$, modulo $10^9 + 9$.

- **Constraints**: $T \le 100$, $1 \le m \le 100$, $0 \le K \le 10^{18}$, Time Limit $1.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: The recurrence $w_{2n} = w_n, w_{2n+1} = 1 - w_n$ is the exact definition of the **Prouhet–Thue–Morse word** $\mathbf{t} = \mu(\mathbf{t})$ under $\mu(\texttt{0}) = \texttt{01}, \mu(\texttt{1}) = \texttt{10}$! Unlike `CP-VII-08` (which asks how many times a fixed $P$ occurs inside a finite iterate $\varphi^k(S_0)$), here we ask how many *distinct extensions* $W$ of length $K \le 10^{18}$ make $S + W$ a valid factor of the infinite word $\mathbf{t}$.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Every factor of $\mathbf{t} = \mu(\mathbf{t})$ starts at either an **even index** $2i$ or an **odd index** $2i + 1$ in $\mathbf{t}$, which corresponds to grouping consecutive pairs of bits and applying the inverse morphism $\mu^{-1}(\texttt{01}) = \texttt{0}, \mu^{-1}(\texttt{10}) = \texttt{1}$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Suppose we want to count valid extensions $W$ of length $K$ for $(S, K)$:

1. **Even-Start Alignment**: $S + W$ starts at an even index $2i$ in $\mathbf{t}$ iff every aligned pair $(S[1]S[2]), (S[3]S[4]), \dots$ belongs to $\{\texttt{01}, \texttt{10}\}$.
   - If $m = |S|$ is even, $S$ decodes uniquely to $S_{\text{even}} = \mu^{-1}(S)$ of length $m/2$, and $W$ is formed by taking a valid extension $W'$ of length $\lceil K / 2 \rceil$ of $S_{\text{even}}$: if $K$ is even, each $W'$ gives $1$ word $\mu(W')$; if $K$ is odd, the last bit of $W'$ is only half-used (contributing $1$ bit, so each $W'$ of length $(K+1)/2$ whose first $(K-1)/2$ bits are expanded by $\mu$ gives $1$ word $W$!).
   - If $m = |S|$ is odd, the last bit $S[m]$ pairs with the **first bit $W[1]$ of $W$**, forcing $W[1] = 1 - S[m]$! Then $S + W[1]$ has even length $m + 1$ and decodes to $S_{\text{even}}$ of length $(m+1)/2$, leaving $K - 1$ bits of $W$ to choose!
2. **Odd-Start Alignment**: $S + W$ starts at an odd index $2i + 1$ in $\mathbf{t}$ iff we prepend $1 - S[1]$ to the front of $S$, shifting it to an even-start alignment of $(1 - S[1]) + S$ with the same $K$!
3. **Why Naive Recursion Double-Counts (`BP-30-05`)**: When can the **same** string $S + W$ occur at *both* an even index and an odd index in $\mathbf{t}$?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
- Recall from **Theorem 30.4 (§2.1 of `Ch 30`)** that in $\mathbf{t}$, equal adjacent bits $\texttt{00}$ and $\texttt{11}$ **only ever occur at odd indices**! Furthermore, $\mathbf{t}$ is cube-free, so it cannot contain $\texttt{010101}$ or $\texttt{101010}$: **every** factor of $\mathbf{t}$ of length $\ge 4$ contains at least one occurrence of $\texttt{00}$ or $\texttt{11}$, which **uniquely locks the index parity (even vs. odd) of the entire factor $S + W$**!
- Conversely, when $|S| + K \le 3$, short alternating factors like $\texttt{010}$ or $\texttt{101}$ do *not* contain $\texttt{00}$ or $\texttt{11}$ and occur at **both** even and odd indices in $\mathbf{t}$!
- **Exact Fix**: Whenever $|S| + K \le 3$, do **not** branch into even + odd decimation! Instead, directly test all $2^K \le 8$ candidate words $W \in \{0, 1\}^K$ against the precomputed set of valid factors of $\mathbf{t}[0..15]$! For $|S| + K \ge 4$, the even-start and odd-start sets of valid words $W$ are **100% disjoint**, so you can simply sum their counts via memoized recursion `solve(S, K)`!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-VII-07"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 30](../chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd) (`T-5B-02`: Prouhet–Thue–Morse Inverse Morphism Parity Decimation $\mu^{-1}$ · `[SDOI2019] 连续子序列` / `Luogu P5362`)**.
- **Proof of Parity Disjointness for $|S| + K \ge 4$**:
  Let $X = S + W$ be any factor of $\mathbf{t}$ of length $L = |S| + K \ge 4$. Could $X$ contain neither $\texttt{00}$ nor $\texttt{11}$? The only binary words of length $4$ avoiding $\texttt{00}$ and $\texttt{11}$ are $\texttt{0101}$ and $\texttt{1010}$.
  - In $\mathbf{t}$, if $\texttt{0101}$ started at an even index $2i$, it would decode under $\mu^{-1}$ to $\texttt{00}$ at index $i$ (which is valid iff $i$ is odd); if $\texttt{0101}$ started at an odd index $2i + 1$, then prepending $1 - \texttt{0} = \texttt{1}$ and appending $1 - \texttt{1} = \texttt{0}$ would give $\texttt{101010}$ at even index $2i$, decoding under $\mu^{-1}$ to $\texttt{111}$—impossible since $\mathbf{t}$ is overlap-free!
  - Symmetrically, $\texttt{0101}$ can *only* start at even indices, $\texttt{1010}$ can *only* start at even indices, and any factor containing $\texttt{00}$ or $\texttt{11}$ at offset $d$ has $(start + d) \equiv 1 \pmod 2$.
  Thus **every factor $X$ of $\mathbf{t}$ of length $L \ge 4$ has a unique starting parity $\bmod 2$ in $\mathbf{t}$**! Consequently, for $|S| + K \ge 4$, the set of extensions $W$ making $S + W$ an even-start factor and the set making $S + W$ an odd-start factor are **strictly disjoint**, so `solve(S, K)` simply adds the two branches without inclusion-exclusion!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-30-05` / `BP-7-08`)**:
  - Cutting off the recursion at $K = 0$ instead of $|S| + K \le 3$ double-counts $S = \texttt{01}, K = 1, W = \texttt{0}$ (since in $\mathbf{t} = \texttt{0110100110010110}\dots$, short factors of length $\le 3$ like $\texttt{010}$, $\texttt{101}$, and $\texttt{01}$ lack $\texttt{00}/\texttt{11}$ parity witnesses and occur at both even and odd indices, e.g., $\texttt{010}$ at odd index $3$ and even index $8$). Stopping at $|S| + K \le 3$ and checking substrings of $T_4 = \texttt{0110100110010110}$ eliminates all short-factor ambiguity.
- **Complexity**: $O(m + \log K)$ states per testcase via `std::map<pair<string, long long>, int>` memoization.
::::

### Problem `CP-VII-08` — Multi-Stage Substitutive Signal Amplification

A signal processor operates over the 4-character alphabet $\Sigma = \{\texttt{'A'}, \texttt{'B'}, \texttt{'C'}, \texttt{'\_'}\}$. Starting from an initial seed string $S_0$ ($1 \le |S_0| \le 50$), each stage $r = 1, 2, \dots, K$ replaces every character $c$ in $S_{r-1}$ simultaneously by its substitution image $\psi(c)$ ($1 \le |\psi(c)| \le 6$). In particular, `'A'`, `'B'`, and `'C'` expand into strings of length $\ge 2$, whereas the spacer character `'_'` is a **fixed point of length $1$**:
$$\psi(\texttt{'\_'}) = \texttt{'\_'}.$$
Given $S_0$, the rules $\psi(c)$, the amplification depth $K$ ($1 \le K \le 10^{18}$), and a target pattern $P[1..m]$ ($1 \le m \le 150$), compute the number of occurrences of $P$ as a contiguous substring of $\psi^K(S_0)$ modulo $10^9 + 7$.

- **Constraints**: $|S_0| \le 50$, $1 \le |\psi(c)| \le 6$, $1 \le m = |P| \le 150$, $1 \le K \le 10^{18}$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: Why does **Regime 1** (`Ch 30` §3.1 — promoting $k_0 = \lceil \log_2 m \rceil$ steps and counting 1-letter and 2-letter factors via a $(|\Sigma| + |\Sigma|^2)$ matrix) **fail completely** here?
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Because $\psi(\texttt{'\_'}) = \texttt{'\_'}$ has length $|\psi^k(\texttt{'\_'})| = 1 < m - 1$ for **every** $k \ge 1$ (`BP-30-02`)! If $\psi(\texttt{'A'}) = \texttt{"A\_"}$, then $\psi^K(\texttt{'A'}) = \texttt{"A"} + \texttt{'\_'}^K$, so an occurrence of $P$ can straddle **up to $m$ consecutive blocks**!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Look at how the KMP Automaton of $P[1..m]$ processes any concatenated string:

- Build the $(m + 1)$-state KMP DFA $\delta(q, c) \in \{0, \dots, m\}$ of $P$ (where reading $P[m]$ from state $m - 1$ increments the match counter by $+1$ and transitions to $\pi[m]$).
- For any string $W \in \Sigma^*$, define its **KMP Automaton Homomorphic Matrix** $M(W)$ of dimension $(m + 2) \times (m + 2)$, where rows/columns $0 \dots m$ represent KMP states $q \in \{0, \dots, m\}$ and column $m + 1$ accumulates match counts:
  - For $q \in \{0, \dots, m\}$: $M(W)_{q,\, \delta^*(q, W)} = 1$, $M(W)_{q,\, m+1} = \operatorname{matches}(q, W)$, and all other entries in row $q$ are $0$.
  - Row $m + 1$ has $M(W)_{m+1,\, m+1} = 1$ and $0$ elsewhere.
- Because $M(U V) = M(U) M(V)$, how does $M(\psi^r(c))$ relate to $M(\psi^{r-1}(x))$ for $x \in \psi(c)$? Since $K \le 10^{18}$ is huge while $M(\psi^r(c))$ is a non-linear recurrence $M(\psi^r(c)) = \prod_{x \in \psi(c)} M(\psi^{r-1}(x))$, we cannot simply raise a single KMP matrix to power $K$; instead, we must run KMP functional composition for $r_0 \approx m$ steps until boundary prefixes and suffixes of length $m - 1$ stabilize, and then switch to a linear recurrence over $L$-step blocks!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
Why did naive Regime 1 ($k_0 = \lceil \log_2 m \rceil$) fail? *Only* because the single spacer letter `'_'` has $|\psi(\texttt{'\_'})| = 1$, while `'A'`, `'B'`, `'C'` all have $|\psi(c)| \ge 2$!
Look at what happens to runs of `'_'` inside $\psi^r(S_0)$:

1. Since $\psi(\texttt{'\_'}) = \texttt{'\_'}$ and every other letter $c \in \{\texttt{'A'}, \texttt{'B'}, \texttt{'C'}\}$ expands to length $\ge 2$ (unless $c$ maps purely to `'_'`s), after at most $r_0 = \lceil \log_2 m \rceil + 3 \le 11$ steps, every expanding letter $c$ has $|\psi^{r_0}(c)| \ge m - 1$!
2. What if an expanding letter like $\psi(\texttt{'A'}) = \texttt{"A\_"}$ generates an unboundedly growing run of `'_'`s ($\psi^r(\texttt{'A'}) = \texttt{"A"} + \texttt{'\_'}^r$)? Notice that any contiguous run of $\ge m$ copies of `'_'` is **completely periodic with period $1$**: once a run of `'_'`s has length $\ge m - 1$, every additional `'_'` beyond $m - 1$ contributes a constant $I_{\text{all-\_}} \in \{0, 1\}$ (1 if $P = \texttt{'\_'}^m$, else $0$) and never changes the $(m-1)$-prefix or $(m-1)$-suffix!
3. Therefore, if we **cap every contiguous run of `'_'`s at length $m$** (tracking separately the total number of `'_'`s if $P = \texttt{'\_'}^m$), or even simpler: after $r_0 \le 11$ steps, every letter $c \in \{\texttt{'A'}, \texttt{'B'}, \texttt{'C'}\}$ whose image contains at least two non-`'_'` letters has length $\ge m - 1$, and any boundary run of `'_'`s grows linearly or exponentially but only its capped length $\min(\text{len}, m - 1)$ affects non-`'\_'^m$ matches!
4. Better yet: what is the **universal clean way** to handle unit-growth letters in Regime 1 for $K \le 10^{18}$?
   - In $\psi^r(S_0)$, view the string as a sequence of **non-spacer letters** $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_L \in \{\texttt{'A'}, \texttt{'B'}, \texttt{'C'}\}$ separated by spacer runs $\texttt{'\_'}^{d_i}$!
   - When $r \to r + 1$, each non-spacer letter $x$ produces a fixed sequence of non-spacer letters with fixed internal spacer gaps, while each existing gap $\texttt{'\_'}^d$ between $x$ and $y$ simply absorbs the trailing `'_'`s of $\psi(x)$ and leading `'_'`s of $\psi(y)$: $d_{\text{new}} = \operatorname{trail}(x) + d + \operatorname{lead}(y)$!
   - Since any gap $d \ge m - 1$ acts identically to $d = m - 1$ for every pattern $P \ne \texttt{'\_'}^m$ (and after at most $m$ steps, any growing gap reaches $\ge m - 1$!), we only ever need to track gap lengths up to $\min(d, m - 1)$—which stabilizes after $r_0 = m + 3 \le 155$ steps!
   - Thus we can run **Regime 2 ($O(m)$ KMP functional composition $f_{\psi^r(c)}$)** for the first $r_0 = \min(K, m + 3)$ steps in $O(|\Sigma| |\psi| m^2)$ time, and if $K > r_0$, every block $\psi^{r_0}(c)$ ($c \in \{\texttt{'A'}, \texttt{'B'}, \texttt{'C'}\}$) has stabilized $(m-1)$-prefix and $(m-1)$-suffix, so **Regime 1's $(|\Sigma| + |\Sigma|^2)$ matrix exponentiation** finishes the remaining $K - r_0$ steps in $O(|\Sigma|^6 \log K)$ time!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-VII-08"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 30](../chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd) (`T-5B-03`: Hybrid Regime 1 + Regime 2 Iterated Morphic Pattern Counting with Unit-Growth Stabilization)**.
- **Complete Structural Synthesis (Why $r_0 = m + 3$ Stabilizes All Boundary Prefixes and Suffixes)**:
  For each letter $c \in \Sigma$, consider the sequence of iterates $W_r(c) = \psi^r(c)$.
  - In **Phase 1 ($1 \le r \le r_0 = \min(K, m + 3)$)**: We do not build the strings $W_r(c)$ explicitly (as they can reach length $6^{150}$). Instead, for each $(r, c)$ we maintain:
    1. Its **KMP Functional Transition Table** $f_{r, c}(q) = (\text{nxt}_{r,c}[q], \text{cnt}_{r,c}[q])$ for $q \in \{0, \dots, m\}$, computed in $O(|\psi(c)| \cdot m)$ time by composing $f_{r-1, x}$ for $x \in \psi(c)$; and
    2. Its exact prefix $\operatorname{pref}_{m-1}(W_r(c))$ and suffix $\operatorname{suff}_{m-1}(W_r(c))$ clamped to length $\le m - 1$!
  - If $K \le r_0$: we simply compose $f_{K, c}$ across the characters $c \in S_0$ starting from KMP state $q = 0$ and output the accumulated match count!
  - If $K > r_0$: why have $\operatorname{pref}_{m-1}(W_r(c))$ and $\operatorname{suff}_{m-1}(W_r(c))$ stabilized (or entered a period dividing $|\Sigma|!$) by $r_0 = m + 3$? Because even if a letter has unit-growth prefix $\psi(c) = \texttt{'\_'} + c$ (growing by $+1$ character per step), after $m - 1$ steps its prefix of length $m - 1$ is completely filled with $\texttt{'\_'}^{m-1}$!
  - Therefore, in **Phase 2 ($r_0 \to K$)**: we use the **exact bottom-up affine recurrence** over $L$-step blocks:
    For every $r \ge m$, $\operatorname{pref}_{m-1}(W_r(c))$ and $\operatorname{suff}_{m-1}(W_r(c))$ are purely periodic in $r$ with period dividing $L = \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, |\Sigma|) \le 12$! Therefore, for every $r \ge m$, the junction occurrences inside $W_{r+1}(c) = \prod_{x \in \psi(c)} W_r(x)$ depend **only on $r \bmod L$**:
    $$\operatorname{occ}(P, W_{r+1}(c)) = \sum_{x \in \psi(c)} \operatorname{occ}(P, W_r(x)) + \operatorname{Junc}_{r \bmod L}(c),$$
    where $\operatorname{Junc}_{r \bmod L}(c)$ is the number of occurrences of $P$ in $W_{r+1}(c)$ that cross at least one boundary between the $|\psi(c)| \le 6$ child blocks $W_r(x_1) \cdots W_r(x_d)$—computed directly by running KMP on the glued boundary windows (dropping internal matches inside each $W_r(x_i)$)! Since this is an affine recurrence of dimension $|\Sigma| + 1 = 5$ with period $L \le 12$, multiplying $L$ step matrices and raising to $\lfloor (K - r_0) / L \rfloor$ solves **every** morphism (including mortal and unit-growth letters!) in $O\bigl(|\Sigma| |\psi| m^2 + |\Sigma|^3 \log K\bigr)$ time!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-30-02` / `BP-7-09`)**:
  - Assuming every character $c \in \Sigma$ satisfies $|\psi^{k_0}(c)| \ge m - 1$ fails whenever a unit-growth character $\psi(\texttt{'\_'}) = \texttt{'\_'}$ exists; using the bottom-up affine recurrence $\operatorname{occ}(P, W_{r+1}(c)) = \sum \operatorname{occ}(P, W_r(x)) + \operatorname{Junc}_{r \bmod L}(c)$ after $r_0 = m$ KMP functional steps handles arbitrary combinations of mortal, unit-growth, and expanding letters seamlessly!
- **Complexity**: $O\bigl(|\Sigma| |\psi| m^2 + |\Sigma|^3 \log K\bigr)$ time and $O(|\Sigma| m)$ space.
::::

## 3. Part VII Diagnostic Mastery Rubric & Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-7-01` – `BP-7-10`)

Score your blind diagnostic performance across `CP-VII-01` through `CP-VII-08`:

- **3 points per problem**: Correctly identified the target chapter (`Ch 26`–`Ch 30`), eliminated the lookalike decoy, and wrote down the governing word/group/graph invariant before opening Hint 1 or Hint 2.
- **2 points per problem**: Opened Hint 1 to resolve a decoy pair, then derived the invariant independently.
- **1 point per problem**: Needed Hint 2 or Hint 3 to assemble the pushdown, BEST formula, or morphic recurrence.
- **0 points**: Opened the complete solution early or fell into one of the ten Part VII boundary pitfalls below.

| Total Score (out of 24) | Diagnostic Readiness | Recommended Action Before the Capstones |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **19 – 24 pts** | **Grandmaster Part VII Mastery** | Advance to the **[Grandmaster Multi-Part Synthesis Capstone (`Syn-01`–`Syn-30`)](../capstones/synthesis.qmd)**. |
| **13 – 18 pts** | **Solid with Decoy Vulnerability** | Re-read Tables 1.1–1.3 and review the specific chapter (`Ch 26`–`Ch 30`) where a decoy or boundary trap caught you. |
| **< 13 pts** | **Structural Rebuild Needed** | Re-work the 4-Step derivations in [Ch 26](../chapters/ch26-word-equations-signed-parallel-dsu.qmd)–[Ch 30](../chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd) and audit every pitfall below. |

### Complete Part VII Boundary Pitfall Checklist (`BP-7-01` – `BP-7-10`)

| Pitfall ID | Chapter | Broken Shortcut / Implementation Bug | Exact Counterexample & Structural Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`BP-7-01`** | `Ch 26` | Returning early in `unite(k, x, y, 1)` when `rx == ry` without setting `is_pal[k][rx] = 1` (`CP-VII-01`). | On $N = 4$ with $S[1..4] = S[1..4]^R$, `rx == ry` at $k = 2$; returning early leaves $4$ components instead of $2$. Always set `is_pal[k][rx] \|= (dx ^ dy ^ d)`. |
| **`BP-7-02`** | `Ch 29` | Using un-indexed $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ + 1D balance $\ge 0$ to test multi-type directed Dyck words (`CP-VII-02`). | On `(( ] [ ))`, 1D balance is $[1,2,1,2,1,0] \ge 0$ and $M_2^{-1}M_2 = I_2$ cancels `] [`! Use Segment-Tree $C^{-1}O$ binary-lifting LCE or height-indexed generators. |
| **`BP-7-03`** | `Ch 27` | Accepting an inverse KMP $\pi$ or Manacher array after checking only local bounds $\pi[i] \le \pi[i-1]+1$ (`CP-VII-03`). | $\pi = [0, 1, 0, 1, 1]$ forces $S = \texttt{aabaa}$, whose true KMP array is $[0, 1, 0, 1, \mathbf{2}]$. Always run forward KMP/Z/Manacher on the reconstructed string! |
| **`BP-7-04`** | `Ch 28` | Dividing the AC-DFA BEST formula by $\prod_{u, v} A(u, v)!$ instead of $\prod_{u, c} C[u][c]!$ (`CP-VII-04`, `UOJ #607`). | When $c_1 \ne c_2$ transition $u \to v$, swapping $u \xrightarrow{c_1} v$ and $u \xrightarrow{c_2} v$ produces **distinct strings**. Divide by $\prod_{u, c} C[u][c]!$. |
| **`BP-7-05`** | `Ch 28` | Including self-loops $u \to u$ on the diagonal of $L_{\text{out}}$, or omitting them from $(\operatorname{outdeg}(u)-1)!$ (`CP-VII-04`). | Self-loops cancel in the arborescence Laplacian $L_{\text{out}}$, but **must** be included in $\operatorname{outdeg}(u)$ inside the BEST factorial $(\operatorname{outdeg}^+(u)-1)!$. |
| **`BP-7-06`** | `Ch 29` | Omitting the $\sqrt{M}$ threshold on child-subtree subtractions in `[CTSC2010] 珠宝商` (`CP-VII-05`). | $200$ children of size $250$ would trigger $200 \times M$ Link-Tree sweeps. Use $O(\|T_{\text{sub}}\|^2)$ DFS whenever $\|T_{\text{sub}}\| \le \sqrt{M}$. |
| **`BP-7-07`** | `Ch 28` | Using 32-bit integers for RLBWT run lengths or LF offsets when $N \le 10^{18}$ (`CP-VII-06`). | Run lengths $L_i$ and character buckets $C[c]$ exceed $2^{31}-1$; use 64-bit `long long` throughout the Move Structure. |
| **`BP-7-08`** | `Ch 30` | Recursing all the way to $K = 0$ in Thue–Morse $\mu^{-1}$ decimation (`CP-VII-07`, `[SDOI2019]`). | Factors of length $\le 3$ like `010` lack `00`/`11` and occur at both even and odd indices. Cut off at $\|S\| + K \le 3$ and check $T_4$ directly. |
| **`BP-7-09`** | `Ch 30` | Applying Regime 1 (fixed $k_0$ 2-letter junction matrix) when unit-growth letters $\psi(\texttt{'\_'}) = \texttt{'\_'}$ exist (`CP-VII-08`). | $\|\psi^k(\texttt{'\_'})\| = 1 < m - 1$ forever. Use $r_0 = m$ KMP functional composition steps followed by the $L$-periodic bottom-up affine recurrence. |
| **`BP-7-10`** | `Ch 30` | Assuming Fibonacci word $F_k$ is a palindrome, or using 1 ramp instead of 2 on $[f_k+1, f_{k+1}]$ (`[周任飞 2017]`). | Only the central word $\pi_k$ ($F_k = \pi_k x y$) is a palindrome; Rytter's singular word $w_{k-1}$ first finishes at $m = f_k + f_{k-2}$, splitting the LRS ramp in two. |
